extracted.intended_audience: railroads, regulatory compliance officers, attorneys and stakeholders who follow FRA rulemaking and 49 CFR part 229
extracted.subtask_description: Final rulemaking document making administrative updates to 49 CFR part 229 (railroad locomotive safety standards), describing specific textual amendments and explaining applicability of notice-and-comment and various regulatory analyses (E.O. reviews, RFA, NEPA, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: APA notice-and-comment exemption for agency organization/procedure/practice rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Administrative Procedure Act (APA), an agency may waive the normal notice and comment procedures if the action is a rule of agency organization, procedure, or practice. (5 U.S.C. 553(b)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document states this final rule merely makes miscellaneous, administrative updates (e.g., updating web addresses) and therefore would not benefit from public comment; notice and comment is not necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: APA 'good cause' waiver for notice-and-comment
rubrics_metrics.description: The APA allows an agency to waive notice and comment when the agency for good cause finds that notice and public procedure are impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest. (5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule relies on this statutory provision as an alternate basis for not providing notice and comment where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) applicability tied to notice-and-comment exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: The RFA requires a regulatory flexibility analysis describing effects on small entities unless the rule is exempt from notice and comment rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because FRA determined this rule is exempt from notice and comment, a regulatory flexibility analysis is not required for this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act — information collection determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must identify whether rules impose new information collection requirements under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (44 U.S.C. 3501-3520).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule contains no new information collection requirements and therefore imposes no PRA burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA categorical exclusion for planning/administrative rulemakings
rubrics_metrics.description: Under NEPA and DOT NEPA Order, certain planning and administrative activities that do not involve or lead directly to construction are categorically excluded (citing 23 CFR 771.118(c)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRA determined this rule is categorically excluded and is not anticipated to result in any environmental impacts; no further NEPA analysis required absent unusual circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism analysis threshold (E.O. 13132)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must consider Federalism implications and prepare a Federalism Assessment if a rule will have a substantial effect on the States or on the distribution of power and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRA concluded the final rule will not have a substantial effect on States or intergovernmental relationships; thus, a Federalism Assessment is not warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The Unfunded Mandates Reform Act requires a written statement if a rule will result in aggregate expenditures of $100,000,000 or more (adjusted for inflation) in any one year by State/local/tribal governments or the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRA determined this final rule will not meet that threshold; therefore no written statement under the Act is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy impact assessment threshold (E.O. 13211)
rubrics_metrics.description: E.O. 13211 requires agencies to prepare a Statement of Energy Effects for any 'significant energy action' that significantly affects energy supply, distribution, or use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRA evaluated the rule and determined it is not a 'significant energy action' and thus no Statement of Energy Effects is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal consultation requirement (E.O. 13175)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must evaluate whether a rule has substantial direct effects on Indian tribes, imposes substantial direct compliance costs on tribal governments, or preempts tribal law, and when required prepare a tribal summary impact statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRA determined the final rule would not have substantial direct effects on tribes or impose substantial direct compliance costs; tribal consultation requirements therefore do not apply and no tribal summary impact statement is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: International trade impact consideration (Trade Agreement Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must avoid creating unnecessary obstacles to foreign commerce and consider international standards where appropriate; the Trade Agreement Act requires consideration of such impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rulemaking is purely domestic in nature and is not expected to affect trade opportunities for U.S. or foreign firms; no international-trade adjustments are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: E.O. 12866 / OMB significance review
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must evaluate rules under Executive Order 12866 and DOT regulatory policies; OMB/OIRA determines whether a final rule is a 'significant regulatory action' under section 3(f) of E.O. 12866.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OIRA determined this final rule is not a significant regulatory action. FRA's evaluation concluded administrative changes impart no additional burdens and provide clarifying benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: E.O. 14192 deregulatory action identification
rubrics_metrics.description: E.O. 14192 requires that for each new regulatory action at least ten prior regulations be identified for elimination; implementation guidance defines 'E.O. 14192 deregulatory action' and 'regulatory action'. An E.O. 14192 deregulatory action is finalized and has total costs less than zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRA states this final rule is expected to have total costs less than zero and therefore would be considered an E.O. 14192 deregulatory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority citation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rules must include the statutory and regulatory authority citations that support the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend §229.7 — penalty reference structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace references to specific penalty amounts in §229.7(b) with general references to 'the minimum civil monetary penalty', 'ordinary maximum civil monetary penalty', and 'aggravated maximum civil monetary penalty', and refer readers to 49 CFR part 209, appendix A for specified amounts updated for inflation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also update web address from www.fra.dot.gov to https://railroads.dot.gov/. The revised paragraph explicitly states penalties apply per violation, each day a violation continues is a separate offense, and FRA's website contains a statement of agency civil penalty policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend §229.7 — conditions for assessing individual/aggravated penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties may be assessed against individuals only for willful violations; an aggravated maximum civil monetary penalty may be assessed per violation where a grossly negligent violation, or a pattern of repeated violations, has created an imminent hazard of death or injury to persons; or a death or injury has occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This language clarifies thresholds for individual and aggravated penalty assessments and cross-references 49 CFR part 209, appendix A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend §229.125(f) — delegation and disapproval process
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise the last sentence to replace 'FRA's Associate Administrator for Safety or any one of FRA's Regional Administrators' with 'FRA's Associate Administrator for Railroad Safety or FRA's Motive Power and Equipment Division Staff Director.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: ensure information gets to the agency subject matter expert in the specific discipline. Any exception from use of auxiliary lights at a specific public grade crossing can be disapproved for a stated cause by those officials after investigation by FRA and opportunity for response from the railroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date specification for final rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rules must state the effective date when amendments take effect.
